stories.title: Vornado Reports Strong Q3 Cash Flow, Revenue Behind Brisk Office Leasing
stories.excerpt: Vornado Realty Trust’s leadership argued Tuesday that the firm has rarely been healthier as it reported positive leasing and robust capital markets metrics. During an Election Day third-quarter earnings call, Vornado reported that funds from operations (FFO) hit $126.6 million in the three months ending Sept. 30, compared to $114.5 in the prior year’s third quarter. Revenue rose as well, increasing to $467.6 million in the third quarter, compared to the $453.7 million the firm reported in the same period one year ago. Vornado also reported a net loss of $47.1 million, compared to net income of $11.5 million over the same period in 2025, a metric that is more reflective of depreciation and amortization within the office- and retail-focused real estate investment trust’s broader portfolio. “We had another excellent quarter with eye-catching mark-to-market results, thanks to our same-store growth,” said Steven Roth, CEO of Vornado Realty Trust, who noted that comparable FFO was up 14 percent from last year’s third quarter. “Everyone’s metrics were pretty good, but our metrics were outstanding.” In the first nine months in 2026, the firm leased 1.6 million square feet, with Manhattan office deals averaging $113 per square foot in starting rents. In the third quarter, Vorando executed 30 office deals totaling 489,000 square feet, with an industry-leading average starting rent of $123 per square foot and an average lease term of 9.5 years. Moreover, its New York office same-store net operating income was up 11.9 percent. “Our budgets show this strong performance will continue through 2028,” said Roth. “The New York office market is by far the strongest in the country and maybe even the strongest it’s ever been.” Roth noted that Manhattan office leasing volume rose 9 percent over the last year, reaching its highest total leasing metrics since 2000. During the third quarter, overall Manhattan office leasing was 10 million square feet, exceeding five-year and 10-year quarter
bullets: Vornado Q3 FFO $126.6M, up 14% YoY; revenue $467.6M vs $453.7M prior year
Office and retail REIT reports 'eye-catching mark-to-market results' and same-store growth
Strong capital markets and leasing metrics signal continued office tenant demand
stories.summary: Vornado reported Q3 FFO of $126.6 million, up 14% year-over-year, with revenue reaching $467.6 million. CEO Steven Roth highlighted excellent comparable FFO growth and strong mark-to-market results, crediting same-store portfolio growth. Despite a net loss of $47.1 million (driven by depreciation), the REIT emphasized robust capital markets and positive office leasing activity.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily developers. Vornado's office and retail focus differs from multifamily fundamentals; however, sustained office demand and capital availability in major markets (NYC, DC, South Florida) may indicate healthy mixed-use development environments where office anchors support surrounding residential. Office strength does not directly drive multifamily supply or demand dynamics.

stories.title: Nuveen Sells South Florida Rental for $53M
stories.excerpt: Nuveen Real Estate sold a multifamily property in Broward County, Fla., for $52.6 million after nearly a decade of ownership, property records show. Legacy Residential Group purchased the 268-unit asset, called Landings at Coconut Creek. The 242,178-square-foot property is at 4854 Fishermans Drive, just south of West Sample Road, about a mile and half west of the Florida Turnpike, in Coconut Creek. TD Bank supplied a $35.5 million acquisition loan to the Miami-based buyer. The sale comes out to just over $196,000 per unit. Built in 1986, the 22-acre property features 22 two-story buildings as well as a pool and a tennis court. Nuveen — the real estate investment arm of Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America — purchased the complex for $45.3 million in 2017. The Chicago-based investment firm has been selling off some of its multifamily assets in South Florida. Last year, the firm sold a 358-unit apartment complex in Miami Gardens for $93.5 million to Greystar. In 2024, it offloaded a 197-unit property in Plantation for $49.4 million, a price that represented a 5 percent loss from its purchase price a decade earlier. Representatives from Nuveen and Legacy Residential Group did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nuveen sold 268-unit Landings at Coconut Creek (Broward) for $52.6M to Legacy Residential
Asset purchased for $45.3M in 2017; sale at $196K/unit signals modest value appreciation over decade
TD Bank provided $35.5M acquisition loan; part of Nuveen's broader South Florida multifamily portfolio exit
stories.summary: Nuveen Real Estate sold the 268-unit Landings at Coconut Creek in Broward County, Florida, for $52.6 million after nine years of ownership, representing a $196,000-per-unit price. The firm purchased the property for $45.3 million in 2017. TD Bank provided a $35.5 million acquisition loan to buyer Legacy Residential Group. Nuveen has been systematically divesting South Florida multifamily assets, having sold three properties in the region since 2024.
stories.impact: Signals Nuveen's strategic exit from South Florida multifamily after modest appreciation (~15% total gain over 9 years, or ~1.4% annualized), suggesting lower-than-expected yield or refinance pressure. The continued institutional seller activity in Broward County creates inventory for smaller operators like Legacy Residential but indicates softening demand or cap-rate compression among long-term holders. South Florida's multifamily market faces headwinds from overbuilding and migration normalization; developers should monitor asset pricing and cap-rate stability in Broward and Miami-Dade.

stories.title: Catalyst IOS Doubles HQ at SL Green’s 800 Third Avenue to 12K SF
stories.excerpt: Catalyst IOS, an investment manager specializing in industrial outdoor storage (IOS), has doubled the size of its 800 Third Avenue headquarters, Commercial Observer has learned. Catalyst’s new 12,000-square-foot office takes up the entire 35th floor of SL Green Realty’s Midtown East Manhattan tower. The company will move from its current 6,000-square-foot space on the 27th floor, according to a company spokesperson. The deal carries a five-year term, and the asking rent was not disclosed. Asking rents for Class A offices in the Grand Central submarket averaged $82.64 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers. The move will support Catalyst’s 37-member team as it grows its platform, which currently comprises over $1.4 billion in assets under management across more than 220 U.S. properties, according to a spokesperson. “As our network of irreplaceable IOS sites and best-in-class team continues to grow, this expanded space will help us achieve our mission of being the sector-defining company in IOS,” Max Heiden, co-founder and partner at Catalyst, said in a statement. Catalyst reported $181 million of completed IOS acquisitions in the first half of 2026. It launched a $400 million equity fund in February — the AV- and EV-focused acquisition strategies of which it discussed with CO in March — and secured a $281 million portfolio financing package in June. Cushman & Wakefield’s Harry Blair, Kyle Cohen and Kelli Berke negotiated the deal on behalf of SL Green, while Catalyst was represented in-house. The firm plans to take occupancy in its new office space by the end of the year. The 526,124-square-foot building, located between East 49th and East 50th streets, also hosts financial planning company Reid Tax & Advisory Services, investment adviser Kimelman & Baird and Silicon Valley-based law firm Ropers Majeski. A spokesperson for C&W did not respond to a request for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver
bullets: Catalyst IOS doubled HQ at SL Green's 800 Third Avenue, Midtown East, to 12,000 SF
5-year lease at $82.64/SF average asking rent (Class A Grand Central submarket Q3 2026)
Catalyst manages $1.4B AUM across 220+ industrial outdoor storage properties; 37-person team expansion
stories.summary: Catalyst IOS, an industrial outdoor storage investment platform with $1.4 billion in AUM across 220+ U.S. properties, expanded its Manhattan headquarters from 6,000 to 12,000 square feet on the 35th floor of SL Green's 800 Third Avenue. The five-year lease at asking rates averaging $82.64/SF in the Grand Central submarket reflects the company's growth trajectory and ability to absorb premium Manhattan office space.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, Catalyst's growth signals robust capital and institutional interest in alternative real estate sectors (industrial outdoor storage). This capital competition for premium office and asset management platforms may pressure REIT and fund capital allocation away from multifamily into niche but higher-yielding subsectors. SL Green's ability to retain and expand tenants in prime Manhattan suggests continued capital markets strength supporting mixed-use and office-anchored development, though this tilts capital away from core multifamily.

stories.title: Old Millionaire’s Row Makes Way for Billionaire’s Row as Mansion Trades for $42M
stories.excerpt: Even a renewed interest in New York City’s Gilded Age through an HBO drama or a civic effort to prevent development can’t stop a mansion built by the Vanderbilt family from being razed. The wheels kept turning in the saga of the Schieffelin-Bowne House, a historic mansion at 35 West 57th Street that dates back to 1891. The Soloviev Group filed a deed transfer of the building for $42 million, according to property records made public Monday. Sedesco will take part ownership in the residential and hospitality property being built in its place near 9 West 57th Street, where Soloviev was able to land an undisclosed office tenant paying a record $327.50 per square foot in April. Soloviev Group and Sedesco did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Soloviev Group and Sedesco are building a supertall condominium and hotel structure at the West 57th Street site, complete with 119 units, a 158-room hotel and a 10,212-square-foot restaurant across 63 floors, according to New York YIMBY. William H. Vanderbilt gifted the Beaux Arts mansion at 35 West 57th Street to his granddaughter, Maria Louise Vanderbilt Shepard, when she was married to William Jay Schieffelin. The pair had other wedding gifts provided by President Benjamin Harrison. The couple lived in the five-story home from 1891 to 1899, when it was sold to well-known businessman Samuel W. Bowne. Bowne rose to prominence in his own right in the pharmaceutical industry and as a philanthropist. His family has landmarks dedicated in his honor elsewhere in the city, as his forebears were some of the earliest settlers in Flushing, Queens, going back to the 17th century. Bowne died in the home in 1910, and his wife Nettie lived there until 1930. But at some point in the 20th century, as New York’s wealthiest families migrated north, the first two floors of the mansion were converted into retail space. bullets: Soloviev Group filed deed transfer for 35 West 57th Street mansion demolition for $42M
Supertall mixed-use: 119 condominium units, 158-room hotel, 10,212 SF restaurant on 63 floors
Sedesco partnership; prior Soloviev office lease at nearby 9 West 57th at record $327.50/SF
stories.summary: Soloviev Group acquired the historic Schieffelin-Bowne House at 35 West 57th Street for $42 million to demolish and redevelop as a supertall mixed-use tower. The project will include 119 residential units, a 158-room hotel, and a 10,212-square-foot restaurant across 63 floors. Sedesco will hold part ownership. Soloviev previously secured an office tenant at nearby 9 West 57th paying a record $327.50/SF.
stories.impact: Strong demand signal for ultra-luxury residential in Manhattan's Midtown South/Billionaire's Row submarket, but limited relevance to core multifamily development. The 119-unit high-end condo component targets affluent ownership rather than rental; the hotel and restaurant anchor are lifestyle amenities for the ultra-prime segment. Developer takeaway: Manhattan's premium residential market remains capital-friendly, but this is trophy mixed-use/hospitality-driven development, not workforce or market-rate multifamily. Cap rates and financing terms may differ sharply from core multifamily.

stories.title: Rental Affordability Declines in Most Metros, but Improved Housing Quality is a Factor
stories.excerpt: Rental housing affordability declined in 82% of U.S. metropolitan areas between 2014 and 2023, with renters experiencing the equivalent of an average $256 annual reduction in income after accounting for changes in housing quality. That’s according to a new report released Tuesday by the Mortgage Bankers Association’s Research Institute for Housing America. The report, Housing Demand and the Decline in Rental Housing Affordability, written by Gary Engelhardt, Ph.D. of Syracuse University, examines the role of housing demand in declining rental affordability. It introduces a new approach to measuring affordability that accounts for changes in housing quality, rental prices and household economic decisions. “Traditional measures of rental affordability often fail to distinguish between rent increases driven by improvements in housing quality and those driven by rising housing costs,” said Engelhardt. “Our research finds that while rental housing affordability declined in most of the country, as much as half of the increase in rental expenditures over the past decade is associated with improvements in housing quality.” The post Rental Affordability Declines in Most Metros, but Improved Housing Quality is a Factor appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Rental affordability declined in 82% of U.S. metros between 2014 and 2023
Average annual rental cost burden equivalent to $256 income reduction after housing quality adjustment
~50% of rent increases tied to improved housing quality, not pure cost inflation
stories.summary: A new Mortgage Bankers Association Research Institute report by Syracuse University's Gary Engelhardt finds that rental affordability fell in 82% of U.S. metropolitan areas from 2014 to 2023, equivalent to an average $256 annual income loss per renter. The study introduces a quality-adjusted affordability metric showing that approximately half of rent growth over the past decade reflects improvements in housing quality (e.g., newer units, amenities) rather than pure cost escalation.
stories.impact: Critical demand signal: declining nominal affordability masks strong underlying demand for higher-quality, newer rental stock. Developers building class-A or high-amenity properties can command rent premiums justified by unit and community quality, supporting higher yields and justifying development. Conversely, older, lower-quality stock faces pressure if it does not upgrade. This suggests continued strong fundamentals for new supply in growth metros and selective repositioning opportunities, but signals risk for aging, non-renovated assets. Supply continues to matter; quality-adjusted demand remains robust despite affordability headline risk.

stories.title: Stream Realty Partners Expands Services into Richmond
stories.excerpt: Stream Realty Partners has expanded its construction and project management capabilities into Richmond, Virginia, with the appointment of Stephen Jayjock as Managing Director of Construction Management. The strategic expansion strengthens Stream’s presence in the Commonwealth and extends its ability to serve occupiers, owners, and investors throughout Central Virginia. In his new role, Jayjock will lead the growth of Stream’s construction and project management services across the Richmond region, focusing on client relationships, project delivery, and team development. Working alongside Managing Director Charlie Smiroldo and Executive Managing Director and Partner Kyle Luby, who oversees Stream’s Washington, D.C., and Northern Virginia offices, Jayjock will leverage the firm’s integrated national platform to provide clients with strategic guidance and hands-on project oversight from initial planning through completion. “Richmond represents an exciting opportunity to expand our construction and project management capabilities and better serve clients throughout Central Virginia,” said Luby. The post Stream Realty Partners Expands Services into Richmond appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Stream Realty Partners appointed Stephen Jayjock as Managing Director of Construction in Richmond, VA
Strategic expansion of construction and project management capabilities into Central Virginia
Coordinates with Charlie Smiroldo (Richmond) and Kyle Luby (DC/Northern Virginia leadership)
stories.summary: Stream Realty Partners expanded its construction and project management services into Richmond, Virginia, with the appointment of Stephen Jayjock as Managing Director of Construction Management. The move strengthens Stream's presence across Central Virginia and leverages the firm's integrated national platform to serve occupiers, owners, and investors. Jayjock will work alongside existing Stream leadership in Richmond and the broader Virginia/DC corridor.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Stream's expansion signals growing construction and development activity across Central Virginia and the broader DC/Northern Virginia corridor, but the announcement does not specify multifamily focus. Stream is primarily a brokerage and services firm, not a developer. However, increased construction management bandwidth in Richmond could indicate rising development velocity in the region and suggests growing demand for qualified project delivery partners, which may correlate with stronger multifamily market fundamentals and entitlement activity.

stories.title: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Opens Largest North American Distribution Center in PA
stories.excerpt: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals recently celebrated the ribbon-cutting of its new 160,000-square-foot distribution facility in Upper Macungie Township, Pennysylvania, marking the company’s largest distribution center in North America. Located on a 6.5-acre campus, the facility is the company’s sole U.S. distribution hub. The center’s 45 employees support operations, quality and administration, supporting the shipment of prescription and over-the-counter medicines to 321 locations in 43 states.The India-based company selected the Lehigh Valley site after evaluating 130 properties across multiple states. The Allentown center joins Glenmark’s U.S. headquarters in New Jersey, its manufacturing facility in North Carolina, and Ichnos Glenmark Innovation, the company’s wholly owned biotechnology subsidiary in New York. Lehigh Valley is home to the U.S. headquarters of B. Braun, Olympus, and Sharp, and to operations of Thermo Fisher Scientific, Piramal Critical Care, and OraSure Technologies. Work recently began on the largest life sciences investment in Pennsylvania history, a $3.5 billion pharmaceutical manufacturing campus by Eli Lilly and Company. The post Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Opens Largest North American Distribution Center in PA appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals opened 160,000 SF distribution center in Upper Macungie, Lehigh Valley, PA
Facility on 6.5-acre campus; sole U.S. distribution hub; 45 employees support 321 locations across 43 states
Lehigh Valley hosts HQs of B. Braun, Olympus, Sharp; Eli Lilly opening $3.5B pharma manufacturing campus
stories.summary: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals completed a 160,000-square-foot distribution facility in Upper Macungie Township, Lehigh Valley, Pennsylvania, representing the company's largest North American distribution center and sole U.S. distribution hub. The firm selected the site after evaluating 130 properties across multiple states. The Lehigh Valley region is increasingly a life sciences and industrial hub, with major tenants including B. Braun, Olympus, Sharp, Thermo Fisher Scientific, and a $3.5 billion Eli Lilly pharmaceutical manufacturing campus under construction.
stories.impact: Significant indirect positive signal for Lehigh Valley multifamily demand. Glenmark's 45-employee distribution hub, combined with major pharma/life sciences tenant concentration (B. Braun, Olympus, Eli Lilly $3.5B campus), suggests sustained employment growth and in-migration to Lehigh Valley. The Eli Lilly project alone will drive thousands of construction jobs and permanent positions, creating demand for both workforce and management-level rental housing. Developers should prioritize Lehigh Valley market entry ahead of Eli Lilly ramp (likely 2025–2027 hiring waves); supply pipeline must be assessed for adequacy relative to pharma/life sciences job growth.

stories.title: Discipline Is the Bridge Between Ambition and Achievement
stories.excerpt: Over the past several weeks, I have had the privilege of delivering keynote speeches about what I call “The DNA of Success,” a framework built around five characteristics that I believe are essential to achieving extraordinary results: passion, discipline, curiosity, expertise and becoming. In my previous column, I explored passion, the first of these characteristics, and why loving what you do provides the fuel necessary for a long and fulfilling career. But passion alone is not enough. I have known many extraordinarily passionate people who never came close to achieving their potential. They had enthusiasm, ambition, intelligence and tremendous dreams, but they lacked one characteristic necessary to convert those aspirations into meaningful accomplishments: discipline. Robert Knakal. PHOTO: Patrick McMullan/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images If passion is the fuel that powers success, discipline is the engine that converts that fuel into forward motion. It is the bridge between what we want to accomplish and what we actually accomplish. I have spent more than 42 years selling investment properties in New York City, and one of the most important lessons I have learned is that success is rarely the product of one extraordinary effort. More often, it is the cumulative result of thousands of ordinary efforts performed with extraordinary consistency. In our business, there is nothing particularly glamorous about making prospecting calls, updating ownership records, studying comparable sales, following up with property owners, or preparing for meetings. These activities rarely generate applause, and many produce no immediate financial reward. Yet they are precisely the activities that create the foundation for long-term achievement. The difference between an average professional and an exceptional one is frequently not what they know or what they are capable of doing. It is what they actually do, consistently, day after day, year after year, regardless of how they feel.
bullets: Opinion column on 'DNA of Success' framework: passion, discipline, curiosity, expertise, becoming
Author reflects on 42 years selling investment properties in New York City
Discipline identified as bridge between ambition and achievement; passion alone insufficient
stories.summary: A thought leadership piece on professional success, emphasizing five characteristics: passion, discipline, curiosity, expertise, and becoming. The author, a 42-year New York real estate veteran, argues that discipline converts passion into results and is essential to converting aspirations into accomplishments.
stories.impact: No material impact to multifamily development fundamentals, supply, demand, capital, or costs. This is an opinion/cultural essay without market-moving data or actionable intelligence on markets, financing, or development feasibility.

stories.title: Martin Selig Real Estate Restructures $500M in Debt for Seattle Office Buildings
stories.excerpt: Martin Selig Real Estate has completed loan modifications totaling nearly $500 million for 12 Seattle office buildings. Newmark leases the portfolio, with a team led by Executive Managing Directors Cavan O’Keefe and Jesse Ottele and Director Brody O’Keefe, working with Martin Selig Real Estate’s Leasing Director Michael Brixner. “These modifications send a clear signal to the market that these assets are actively competing for tenants,” said O’Keefe. The modifications cover nine buildings financed through a loan serviced by Midland Loan Services, along with three additional buildings financed under a separate loan facility. Under the executed Midland agreement, the receivership will be terminated and the loan transferred back to the master servicer before the end of 2026. Collectively, the modifications position ownership and Newmark to accelerate leasing activity. The 12 buildings total approximately 2.2 million square feet across the Central Business District, Waterfront, Belltown, Lower Queen Anne and Ballard The post Martin Selig Real Estate Restructures $500M in Debt for Seattle Office Buildings appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Martin Selig Real Estate completed $500M loan modifications for 12 Seattle office buildings
Portfolio totals ~2.2M SF across CBD, Waterfront, Belltown, Lower Queen Anne, Ballard
Midland Loan Services receivership termination and transfer back to master servicer by end-2026
stories.summary: Martin Selig Real Estate completed nearly $500 million in loan modifications across 12 Seattle office buildings totaling approximately 2.2 million square feet. The modifications cover nine buildings financed through Midland Loan Services (receivership to be terminated and loan transferred by end-2026) and three additional buildings under a separate facility. Newmark is leasing the portfolio.
stories.impact: Modest indirect signal on capital and financing conditions. Loan modifications rather than defaults suggest lenders are working with sponsors to stabilize distressed Seattle office assets; this indicates capital markets willingness to restructure (rather than foreclose) and suggests floor under office valuations. However, the modification need itself signals Seattle office distress (post-tech-downturn, hybrid work headwinds). Multifamily developers should note: if office is struggling in Seattle despite Amazon/tech concentration, multifamily demand may face headwinds if those office tenants contract or relocate. Monitor Seattle multifamily absorption and rent growth; office weakness does not always predict residential softness but warrants caution.

stories.title: Gantry Secures Financing for S. Arizona Golf Resort
stories.excerpt: Gantry secured $27.9 million in structured financing for the acquisition of Tubac Golf Resort & Spa, located in Tubac, Ariz. The AAA Four Diamond resort sits on more than 500 acres of the historic Otero Ranch, about 45 miles south of Tucson with ready access to I-19. It features 98 rooms and suites, including 17 private casitas, a 27-hole golf course, and a full-service spa. Gantry’s Adam Parker and Andrew Christopherson represented the borrower. The financing pairs a 5-year fixed-rate loan from a Regional Bank with a 25-year SBA 504 loan, funded through a Certified Development Company (CDC), in second position. Both loans carry a 25-year amortization. Parker added, “We found the right regional bank and paired it with an SBA 504 structure. The CDC’s loan, secured by a second lien, gave the sponsor a lower cost of capital as opposed to a mezzanine structure.” The post Gantry Secures Financing for S. Arizona Golf Resort appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gantry secured $27.9M structured financing for Tubac Golf Resort & Spa acquisition, Ariz.
98-room AAA Four Diamond resort on 500+ acres; 27-hole golf course; 45 miles south of Tucson
Financing: 5-year fixed regional bank loan + 25-year SBA 504 in second position; 25-year amortization
stories.summary: Gantry secured $27.9 million in structured financing for the acquisition of Tubac Golf Resort & Spa in southern Arizona, approximately 45 miles south of Tucson near I-19. The property comprises 98 rooms and suites (including 17 private casitas), a 27-hole golf course, full-service spa, and sits on over 500 acres. Financing combines a 5-year fixed-rate regional bank loan with a 25-year SBA 504 CDC loan in second position, both on 25-year amortization.
stories.impact: No material impact to multifamily development. Hospitality/resort financing is a distinct sector with different capital sources (SBA 504, regional banks, specialty lenders) and underwriting than multifamily. This deal signals SBA 504 availability and regional bank appetite for experiential hospitality, but does not reflect multifamily capital conditions, supply, or demand. Developers in Arizona should note regional bank activity and SBA lending appetite as indirect capital market signals, but this transaction does not speak to multifamily-specific financing or market fundamentals.
